text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's parliament speaker Yordan Sokolov said he had submitted information on all deputies to the government commission, which is to open secret police files from the communist era under a bill approved by parliament last month. @

-- Bulgaria's private insurance company Trakia Ins. said it would call a tender for a 47 percent stake of its capital so far held by the private Agrobusinessbank which was declared insolvent on July 14.
-- Bulgarian customs officers at the northern Danube river port of Russe said they had seized 2,432 pirate CD's hidden in a Romanian passenger train.

-- Bulgaria will set a minimum purchase price for lower quality wheat from this year's crop at 210,000 levs after summer rainfalls affected the quality of the wheat, Agriculture minister Ventsislav Varbanov said. The minimum purchase price for first quality wheat is set at 230,000 levs.

-- Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said Bulgaria's annual 1997 inflation is expected at 599 percent and GDP was expected to fall by 5.9 percent. In a report on economic prospects for Central and Eastern Europe Deutsche Morgan Grenfell sees 3.5 percent growth for Bulgaria in 1998.

-- The regional court in the Black Sea port of Varna said it had ruled in favour of a claim by 18 Bulgarians against the Varna-based M & I get-rich-quick investment scheme and had ordered the sale of real estate property of M & I's owner Krasimira Danailova to repay some 35 billion levs M & I owed to 8,348 creditors.
-- Bulgaria's police said it had seized 1,886 videotapes with pornographic films in a raid in Sofia.
